title: Predictive Guard + Telemetry for Dedicated Capacity Fairness (PRD)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated capacity customers require predictable performance and fair access to burst capacity during transient load spikes. Existing reserved pools and hard preemption policies create brittle user experiences: some tenants experience abrupt evictions while others hoard headroom. We lack a unified telemetry-driven mechanism to detect imminent contention, score tenant fairness, and apply controlled, reversible mitigations that preserve SLAs for committed capacity while allowing safe short-term bursting.

Objective: Deliver a Predictive Guard system that: (1) ingests runtime telemetry from Dedicated hosts and the scheduler, (2) computes a tenant fairness score and burst risk per pool, (3) recommends or enacts adaptive soft-lease controls and temporary headroom allocations, and (4) surfaces clear telemetry and rollback controls in the Console. The feature should reduce emergency preemptions by 40% and reduce tail latency regressions for committed tenants by 25% under mixed workloads.

Scope: This PRD covers the behavioral spec, acceptance criteria, telemetry and rollout plan for the Predictive Guard + Telemetry capability. It includes: fairness scoring algorithm, risk thresholds, actions (soft-lease extension, temporary headroom, throttled burst windows), Console UX for visibility and manual override, and alerts/playbooks for oncall. It excludes full scheduler refactors, new billing models for burst credits, and offline capacity forecasting UI (handled in a follow-up).

Constraints: Must work with existing Dedicated autoscaler and reserve APIs, operate within current tenancy isolation primitives, and require no breaking changes to customer-facing reserve contracts. Telemetry ingestion must not materially increase control-plane costs or latency.
user_stories: As a platform engineer, I want an early warning when a pool is likely to run into contention so I can preemptively adjust headroom or notify customers.

As a tenant admin with reserved capacity, I want short-term controlled burst allowance that is transparent and reversible so my critical requests succeed during spikes without violating other tenants' SLAs.
As an oncall, I want clear runbook steps and dashboard widgets showing tenant fairness and recent mitigations so I can quickly assess whether to rollback automated actions.
As a product analyst, I want event-level telemetry indicating fairness score changes, actions taken, and downstream latency impact so I can measure effectiveness of the feature.
requirements: Telemetry pipeline: ingest per-tenant metrics (inflight tokens, queue length, avg token latency, model variant, recent preemptions) at 5s granularity into time-series store.
Fairness scoring: deterministic function combining reserved_fraction, recent_token_consumption_rate, burst_history_decay, and active_request_priority to produce a 0-100 score.
Risk classification: map score + trend to three classes: Green (no action), Amber (recommend prewarm/soft-lease), Red (automated soft-throttle + fallback to lower-cost variant).
Actions: programmatic soft-lease extension (time-limited), temporary headroom carveout (bounded % of pool), and throttled burst windows (rate-limited tail requests).
Console UX: new dedicated tab in Dedicated Capacity -> Pools with time-series of fairness_score, recent_actions, and manual override buttons (recommendation, apply, rollback).
APIs: POST /pools/{id}/predictive-guard/actions to apply/revoke actions and GET /pools/{id}/predictive-guard/status to fetch computed scores and recent recommendations.
Safety: any automated mitigation must include an automatic rollback timer (default 60s) and require explicit opt-in for fully automated mode at pool-level.
Observability: events emitted for every decision containing tenant_id, pool_id, score, inputs, action_taken, operator (auto/manual), and correlation_id.
Permissions: only customers with pool admin role may enable automated mode and perform manual overrides; actions must be recorded in audit logs.
out_of_scope: Long-term billing for burst usage (billing/product work will follow).
Major scheduler architecture rewrite or new autoscaler design.
Per-tenant ML-based forecasting models (this PRD uses lightweight heuristics; model-based predictors are planned later).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Telemetry pipeline populates per-tenant metrics at 5s intervals for 95% of pools in the test cluster without exceeding baseline control-plane CPU by more than 8%.
AC-2: Fairness score computed deterministically from inputs and validated with unit tests across edge cases (zero-reserve, bursty traffic, long-tail requests).

AC-3: Risk classification correctly transitions from Green->Amber->Red for synthetic replay workload within expected thresholds; automation recommends actions at Amber and applies only when pool is opted-in to automated mode.
AC-4: Automated soft-lease and temporary headroom actions can be applied via API and are observable in Console with action metadata and rollback timer.

AC-5: Enabling automated mode requires pool admin consent (Console checkbox) and creates an auditable record; manual override can immediately cancel an automated action and restores pre-action state within 10s.
AC-6: Under mixed-tenant stress test, the number of emergency hard preemptions decreases by >=40% versus the current baseline and committed-tenant p95 token latency improves by >=25%.
AC-7: All mitigation actions emit events that can be queried in the event store and linked to traces in the Console for debugging.
metrics: Committed-tenant p95 token latency during contention (target: -25%)
Average time automated mitigations are active (goal: < 120s)
False-positive mitigation rate (actions when no real contention occurred) < 5%
Telemetry ingestion SLO: 95% of points arrive within 10s
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: Predictive Guard overview showing pools by risk class and recent actions.
Alert: Pool risk enters Red and automated mitigation fails to apply after 10s -> Pager to capacity-oncall.
Alert: Telemetry ingestion lag >20s for >5% of pools -> Pager to infra-oncall.
Log: All action events stored in audit stream and retained per retention policy.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): Enable telemetry and scoring in internal test cluster for 2 weeks, validate metrics and refine thresholds. Phase 2 (customer opt-in): expose recommendation UI + manual apply for a small set of pilot customers (3-5). Phase 3 (automated opt-in): allow pool admins to opt into automated mitigations after pilot success. Each phase gated by acceptance criteria metrics and security review. Rollback procedure: global kill-switch at control-plane and per-pool opt-out.

Schedule: Canary start 2026-04-01, Pilot start 2026-04-20, Automated opt-in broadly available 2026-05-15.
runbook: Documented runbook steps: (1) inspect pool fairness timeline in Console, (2) check recent actions and correllation_id, (3) if mitigation is harmful: click rollback, (4) if mitigation necessary but insufficient: escalate to capacity-oncall to increase reserved headroom, (5) if telemetry lag suspected: restart metrics agent on affected hosts. Playbook linked in artifacts.
risks: Over-eager mitigations could reduce throughput for legitimate bursty tenants (safety mitigated via default opt-in=false and short rollback timers).
Telemetry noise or mis-attribution across multi-tenant workloads could produce false positives (mitigated through decay windows and conservative thresholds).
Increased control-plane load from telemetry ingestion (mitigated by sampling and 5s granularity cap).
Console UX complexity may confuse customers; we will conduct targeted usability tests during pilot.
open_questions: Q1: What is the appropriate default temporary headroom cap as percent of pool? Proposed: 10% capped at 32 GPUs equivalent. Feedback required.
Q2: Should we bill temporary headroom usage immediately or reconcile in a later billing pass? Product/billing decision needed.
Q3: Do we want to expose raw fairness inputs to customers or only the composite score and actions? Security/competitive concern.
